newsitem.title: USA: Lucent's net triples, stock surges.
newsitem.headline: Lucent's net triples, stock surges.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc. blew past Wall Street expectations in its earnings report for the third quarter, posting profits that were triple the amount it reported for the same period a year ago.

The white-hot earnings report from Lucent, the former telecommunications equipment arm of AT&T Corp, drove the stock price up $6 to a new all-time high of $89.375 on the New York Stock Exchange. The stock pulled back slightly, to $88.69, by afternoon.
Lucent's net income rose to $213 million, or 33 cents a share, for the quarter ending June 30, from $72 million or 11 cents a share, in the year-ago June period.
The consensus expectation on Wall Street was for around $160 million, or 25 cents a share, for the latest quarter, according to the First Call service, which compiles analysts' projections.

Lucent, the leading U.S. supplier of telephone equipment, attributed its good fortune to growth among its main customer base of large phone carriers, which are arming themselves for the coming era of head-to-head local and long-distance competition.

"We have been acheiving these results in our core businesses all along, but they've been hidden because we have been restructuring in consumer products and other categories," Chief Finance Officer Don Peterson said in an interview.

Looking to the current quarter ending in September, Peterson said that, despite the typical seasonal purchasing slowdown that occurs during the summer, "We expect to be continue to perform very, very well."

Several analysts said they were preparing to boost their projections for future earnings. Alex. Brown analyst Chris Crespi raised his rating on the stock to "buy" from "market perform" following the earnings report.

Revenues jumped 18.2 percent to $6.34 billion from $5.4 billion, with a 22.6 percent gain in revenues from the company's three core businesses in systems for network operators, microelectronic products and business communications systems.
Revenues from network systems sold to phone network operators grew 27.3 percent to $3.8 billion, Lucent said.
Driving the growth were sales of both phone switches and wireless communications systems, along with sales of fiber optic cable and professional services, the company said.
Growing use of the Internet, data networks and faxes generated strong demand for second lines in businesses and homes and further boosted the group's performance.

Domestic network systems revenues rose 41 percent, with higher sales among all major groups, including traditional customers like the regional Bell companies and newer customers among cellular, cable and competitive local service companies.

In its other two core operating units, Lucent said business communications systems revenues grew 16.3 percent to $1.6 billion and microelectronic, or semiconductor, product revenues rose 13.6 percent to $687 million.
The company also cited progress in controlling costs as a factor behind the strong results. Operating expenses as a percentage of revenues fell to 22.1 percent from 27.4 percent a year ago.

"We are certainly not done with our overhead (cost-cutting) opportunity by any measure," Peterson said. At the time of its spinoff from AT&T, Lucent said it planned to reduce operating expenses to below 20 percent of revenues by 1999.

Lucent, which was spun off to shareholders of AT&T last year after the telephone giant moved to split itself into three companies, has vastly outperformed its former parent. AT&T's stock has been hurt by growing competition in its core long-distance markets and investments it is making in new markets.

NCR Corp., the computer systems company that was the third piece of the former AT&T, reported a loss of $4 million, or 4 cents a share, in the second quarter, down from a loss of $18 million, or 18 cents a share, a year ago.
NCR stock rose $1 to $28.875 on the New York Stock Exchange early afternoon. AT&T was off unchanged at $35, also on the NYSE.
